overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 14
overview.text: In this lesson, you will solve multi-step linear inequalities. While adding or subtracting real numbers preserves the order of inequality, multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the direction of the inequality symbol on the coordinate line.
outcomes: Solve multi-step linear inequalities using the addition and multiplication properties of inequality.
Demonstrate and justify why multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality symbol.
Express solution sets using set-builder notation and graph them on a real number line.
overview.teacherInsight: Illustrate inequality reversal on a real number line with positive numbers: $2 < 5$. Multiplying by $-1$ reflects both numbers across 0 to $-2$ and $-5$. Because $-2$ lies to the right of $-5$, $-2 > -5$.

content.html:
The Negative Multiplier Inequality Direction Flipper

Compare $A < B$. Multiply both numbers by scalar $k$ and observe how multiplying by a negative reverses order.

Multiplier ($k$):k = -1
Initial State ($A = 2, B = 5$) 2 < 5 2 is to the left of 5
Scaled State ($kA$ vs $kB$) -2 > -5 Symbol reversed!
REVERSED: Symbol flipped from < to >
Multiplying by negative reflects positions across the origin.

vocabulary.definition: If a < b and c < 0, then ac > bc. Multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the direction of the inequality symbol.
A mathematical shorthand notation describing a set by stating the properties that its members must satisfy, e.g., {x | x > -9}.

practiceQuestions.question: Solve the inequality $6x - 5 < 7x + 4$ and express the solution in set notation:
practiceQuestions.explanation:
From the official Eureka Math Exit Ticket Key:
$6x - 5 < 7x + 4 \implies -5 < x + 4 \implies -9 < x \implies x > -9$. In set notation: $\{x \text{ real} \mid x > -9\}$.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the rigorous mathematical explanation for why the direction of an inequality reverses when multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number?
options: It is a shortcut for the addition property of inequality: adding terms to the opposite side of zero reflects their positions across the origin.
Negative numbers have no defined order on the real number line.
Flipping the inequality is an arbitrary convention with no algebraic proof.
Because negative numbers are always larger in magnitude than positive numbers.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Consider $-5x > 30$. Adding $5x$ to both sides gives $0 > 5x + 30$. Subtracting 30 gives $-30 > 5x$, and dividing by $+5$ gives $-6 > x$ (or $x < -6$). Flipping the inequality sign shortcuts this exact sequence.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 14 Exit Ticket: Solving Inequalities into Single Variable Systems
exitTicket.prompt: Find the solution set to each inequality. Express the solution in set notation and graphically on the number line: (1) 6x - 5 < 7x + 4, (2) x^2 + 3x - 1 >= x^2 + 5. Fergus asks why the inequality direction reverses when multiplying by a negative number; provide an explanation using the addition property.
exitTicket.solution:
1) 6x - 5 < 7x + 4 => -5 < x + 4 => -9 < x => x > -9. Solution set: {x real | x > -9}.
2) x^2 + 3x - 1 >= x^2 + 5 => 3x - 1 >= 5 => 3x >= 6 => x >= 2. Solution set: {x real | x >= 2}.
Fergus explanation: If -5x > 30, adding 5x and subtracting 30 gives -30 > 5x => -6 > x, or x < -6. Flipping the inequality is simply a shortcut for applying the addition property of inequality.

guidedExercises.title: Example 1: Inequality Direction Reversal Under Negative Operations
guidedExercises.problem: Solve $-4x + 7 < 31$ and graph the solution set. Explain why the inequality symbol reverses when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
guidedExercises.scaffolding: Subtract 7 from both sides, then divide by $-4$. Remember the reflection property across zero on the number line.

steps.label: Divide both sides by $-4$ (Reverse inequality)
steps.explanation: Dividing by a negative reflects positions across zero, reversing relative order.

guidedExercises.finalAnswer: x > -6 \quad (\text{Interval: } (-6, \infty); \text{ Open circle at } -6\text{ with ray right})
guidedExercises.commonPitfall: Reversing the inequality symbol when adding or subtracting negative numbers. The symbol ONLY reverses when MULTIPLYING or DIVIDING by a negative number.

problems.prompt:
Find the solution set for each inequality and express in set notation:
(a) 2x < 10
(b) -15x \ge -45
(c) -5(x - 1) \ge 10
(d) 13x < 9(1 - x)
Prove why multiplying both sides of -2 < 5 by -1 requires reversing the inequality sign to produce a true statement.
problems.solution: On a number line, -2 lies to the left of 5. Multiplying by -1 reflects both numbers across 0 to their opposites: -2 becomes +2, and 5 becomes -5. Since +2 lies to the right of -5, the relationship becomes 2 > -5. The direction of relative position reverses under reflection across the origin.
